story.head: Malott meets his old team
paras: The Ducks (11-11-1) lost 4-0 to Colorado on Nov 19, while the Kings have won two in a row. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kings seventh (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Ducks third (19th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Kings have played better than their record (.400) says: their chances are worth about .615, and their finishing has held them back. The Ducks’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth.

The Kings keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest) and hound the puck on the forecheck (5th). On the other side, the Ducks play fast, open games (4th) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st), so the Kings keep dangerous shots away, but they give up a lot of them. Anaheim has allowed 3.87 goals a game, the third most in the league. Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Adrian Kempe (6 G / 8 A / 14 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Kings’ scoring lead. Alex Laferriere (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 20 GP) shares it. Cutter Gauthier (21 G / 8 A / 29 P in 22 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind.

Darcy Kuemper (7-5-1 / .885 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Los Angeles. Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (4-1-0 / .866 SV% in 5 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-6-1 / .857 SV% in 12 GS). Brossoit has started five of their last ten games, but Dostál got the last one on Nov 19. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
